Inconsistent ﬁndings were also observed for trials examining fruit juice and SSB intake. In a systematic review of 64 observational
studies, SSB intake was associated with higher risk of breast (RR ¼ 1.14, 95%CI 1.01–1.30, n ¼ 7 studies, I2 ¼ 0%) and prostate
(RR ¼ 1.18, 95%CI 1.10–1.27, n ¼ 3 studies, I2 ¼ 0%) cancer (Llaha et al., 2021). A similar (but weaker) association was reported
with fruit juice intake and prostate cancer (RR ¼ 1.03, 95%CI 1.01–1.05, n ¼ 4 studies, I2 ¼ 0%). However, this review observed no
association between SSB or fruit juice and other cancer types such as colorectal, bladder, renal cell, and pancreatic cancers.
Overall, only a very small number of studies reported a link; therefore, the association between sugar intake and cancer risk is
considered weak. Additional evidence is required to conﬁrm this conclusion
